title: Training Notes — Payment Record Courtesy on the Final Month (Independent Living)
content:
A settling residency under the Independent Living Residency Agreement in good payment standing receives a standing courtesy on the final month's base fee charge.

**Rule.** Standing is counted over the late fees and returned payments posted on the residency within the 12 months ending on the day of posting. A residency with no late fee and no returned payment receives 2.0 percent; a residency with exactly one late fee or returned payment in total receives 1.0 percent; any other residency receives none.

**Q. What does "exactly one in total" cover?**
A. One late fee and no returned payment, or one returned payment and no late fee.

**Q. Full table?**

| Late fees within the 12 months | Returned payments within the 12 months | Standing courtesy |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 2.0 percent |
| 1 | 0 | 1.0 percent |
| 0 | 1 | 1.0 percent |
| 1 | 1 | None |
| 2 or more | Any | None |
| Any | 2 or more | None |

**Q. How does it act on the charge?**
A. The courtesy percentage reduces the final month's base fee charge before rounding. Where it is not the only courtesy percentage on the charge, all the courtesy percentages are first added into one total, which reduces the charge once; they never act one after another. The result is rounded once to the cent half up.

**Q. Hypothetical example?**
A. A residency with one returned payment eight months before the day of posting and no late fee receives 1.0 percent; on a charge of 1,500.00 before rounding, with no other courtesy, that is 1,485.00.
